subject: Rasch model with the Newton-Raphson procedure

messages.author: 3a1e6409940a2fd4
messages.subject: Rasch model with the Newton-Raphson procedure
parts:
Hi Dr. Chalmers,

I'm just learning IRT and, for practice, I am trying to recreate a set of difficulty parameters using the standardization dataset for a published test. The test manual indicates that the parameters were derived from a Rasch model using the Newton-Raphson procedure.

When I use mirt(data, 1, itemtype="Rasch", optimizer = 'NR'), R crashes.

I've tried using the default 2PL and constraining the discrimination parameter with
values <- mirt(spss[,15:68],1,pars = 'values')
mirt(data, 1, optimizer = 'NR', constrain = list(values$parnum[values$name == 'a1']))

The discrimination parameter from this second procedure is fixed at 1.28, but the difficulty parameters are very different from the parameters I am trying to replicate. Could this be caused by the shift in the discrimination parameter from 1 to 1.28? Is it possible to constrain the discrimination parameter to 1, or to fit the Rasch model directly using the Newton-Raphson procedure? 

Thanks!
Megan

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Rasch model with the Newton-Raphson procedure
parts:
This is likely a bug as the NR optimizer is rarely used/tested. I'd recommend sticking with the default BFGS family of optimizers as they are more stable Quasi-Newton optimizers rather than true-blue Newton-Raphson, and therefore are more robust during each extrapolated update. In any event, if you could provide a reprex I could look into patching the issue in future versions. Thanks.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Rasch model with the Newton-Raphson procedure
parts:
I see the issue now, and have sent the patch to the dev version on Github. Though I still recommend sticking with the default estimators due to their robustness and efficiency (computing the complete Hessian for each NR iteration can be needlessly expensive). HTH.

Phil
